title: Public Sparse Random Matrix Construction
objective: Wire Sage-compatible sparse random construction into public random_matrix over ZZ, QQ, GF(2), and word GF(p) through one storage-level bulk boundary with competitive warm performance

handoff.summary: Explicit-density random_matrix now dispatches ZZ to an owned FmpzMatrix resource with keep-first collisions, QQ to an owned FmpqMatrix resource with replacement collisions, GF(2) to M4RI Bernoulli fill (or the portable packed representation), and packed small GF(p) to compiler-owned residues with replacement collisions. Five CPython-parseable typed-Python kernels consume and republish the shared seeded stream inside one bulk fill call; native-disabled execution samples the same storage-neutral policy and is seed-identical on fixed witnesses. The 365 added matrix.py lines are intentional orchestration rather than formatting churn: 22 lines declare two lazy modules, about 315 lines allocate canonical domain storage, select one executor/fallback, publish RNG state and traces, and close failed resources, while the remaining hook distinguishes explicit density and preserves Sage edge normalization. Warm 1000x1000 density=0.1 medians on linux-x64 were approximately ZZ 13-23 ms, QQ 16 ms, GF(2) 7 ms, and GF(7) 2.4 ms, competitive with local SageMath medians of about 19, 35, 33, and 2.5 ms respectively.
risks: The native bounded ZZ and QQ executors deliberately support one-word bounds up to 2^32; wider exact bounds retain the existing correct dynamic construction path rather than silently narrowing.
Linux x64 has focused, strict, architecture, native-lifecycle, and benchmark evidence; required non-x64 platforms still need CI execution.

The broad native suite reached and passed FFI/resource lifecycle coverage but later hit a pre-existing foreign-header cache witness assertion unrelated to this diff; focused compilation and resource execution pass.
next_steps: Add test/public-sparse-random.cjs to the shared node test manifest in the integration lane.
Run the focused trace regression after the concurrent matrix-vector trace visibility repair lands.
Consider a declared reciprocal-uniform rational generator before claiming optimized distribution='1/n'; it currently retains the general fallback.
